published_statement: v1 p.6, verbatim from the text layer: '... = K_ab K_mn 12 eps^2/(1+eps^2)^2. (3.7) From this result, Eq. (2.16), and the fact that K_00 = omega/(2L^3), we find that Delta(x) = (10 eps + sqrt2 cos(2 theta))/(12 eps). (3.8) From Eq.(2.16), it follows that the condition for the expectation value of energy density to be negative is cos(2 theta) > sqrt2 eps. In this case we have Delta(x) > 1. This indicates when the energy density is negative, the energy density fluctuations are large and the semiclassical theory is not a good approximation.' with p.5 (3.2): 'Delta(x) = | (<:T00^2(x):> - <:T00(x):>^2) / <:T00^2(x):> | ... Note that we have used normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum state to define the various operators.'
published_hypotheses: H1 massless free scalar field in FLAT (Minkowski) spacetime, stress tensor bilinear (2.11), minimal coupling
H2 a single box-normalised plane-wave mode k (volume L^3), K_00 = omega/(2L^3)
H3 state (2.15) |Psi> = (|0> + eps|2>)/sqrt(1+eps^2), eps REAL 'for simplicity' (p.4)
H4 normal ordering of T00 and of T00^2 against the Minkowski vacuum (p.5)
H5 coincidence limit, purely temporal component: Delta(x) of (3.2), WITH the absolute value
H6 the inference is drawn from KF's own (3.8) (and (2.16) for the sign condition) -- 'In this case we have Delta(x) > 1' is a corollary of (3.8), not an independent computation
hypothesis_drift: SCOPE (named, not a drift against KF): the tree evaluates the claim against the EXACT Delta (fluctuation.py:55-58, 230, 237), not against KF's (3.8). As an inference FROM (3.8) KF's sentence is valid for every real eps != 0, with or without the |.| (re-derivation C8, z3); the fault lies upstream in (3.8), which the tree records separately (KF_38_IS_EXACT = False, fluctuation.py:142). The tree's wording 'With the exact Delta that is FALSE' carries that scope correctly.

UNDERSTATED (in KF's favour, not M's): fluctuation.py:57 says 'z3 finds the counterexample' and data_used names one witness (eps = 1/10, theta = 0). The truth is stronger: with the exact Delta there is NO point of the family with rho < 0 and Delta > 1 (C5, z3 UNSAT with vacuity guard SAT); indeed exact Delta <= 1 on the whole (eps, theta) plane, equality only at (sqrt2, cos2th = -1) and (-sqrt2, +1), both rho > 0 (C4). The claim fails at every rho < 0 point, not at a witness.

DROPPED (harmless): the absolute value of (3.2). The tree's exact Delta is written 1 - (2eps - sqrt2 cos2th)^2/(3(1+eps^2)) without |.| (fluctuation.py:40, 230, 237). On rho < 0 the bracket lies in (1/3, 1), so |.| changes nothing for this claim; on rho > 0 it can reach -1 (C4 equality points), where KF's Delta is +1. The tree's z3 test X^2 > 6(1+eps^2) (fluctuation.py:311) IS the |.|-correct form of 'Delta > 1'.

INHERITED (KF-side discrepancy, harmless for the tree): KF's printed sign condition cos(2theta) > sqrt2 eps is exact only for eps > 0; with eps real as KF state (H3), for eps < 0 the condition reverses to cos2th < sqrt2 eps (C10, z3; counter-point exists). The canonical name 'rho < 0 (cos 2theta > sqrt2 eps)' inherits the eps > 0 presumption, and the tree's sympy uses eps positive (fluctuation.py:175); the tree's z3 hypothesis is the sign-general e(2e - sqrt2 c) < 0 (fluctuation.py:305), so its refutation and T2 hold for all real eps. eps -> -eps is equivalent to theta -> theta + pi/2, so nothing physical moves.

later_literature.ref: B. L. Hu, A. Roura & E. Verdaguer, 'Induced quantum metric fluctuations and the validity of semiclassical gravity', arXiv:gr-qc/0402029
later_literature.what: 'An earlier criterion put forth by Kuo and Ford [5] used the variance of the fluctuations of the stress tensor operator compared to the mean value as a measure of the validity of SCG. As pointed out by Hu and Phillips [27, 28] (see reply by Ford and Wu [7]) such a criterion should be refined by considering the back reaction of those fluctuations on the metric.' Narrows the significance of Delta as a validity criterion (the tree's reason (a)/(b) at fluctuation.py:105-113 runs the same way); says nothing about the specific inequality Delta > 1.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis does not bite on this result, and the evidence is the re-derivation: the claim is a closed-form statement about a single-mode Fock expectation value with NO empirical input (K_00 cancels; C3). Everything needed -- the commutator, the box mode, the state (2.15), the definition (3.2) -- was in Kuo & Ford's hands in 1993, and their own ingredients suffice to see the claim fails: every combination of their printed (2.16)/(3.7) with the exact expressions gives Delta < 1 on rho < 0 (C7). The error is algebraic, entering at (3.8) (C9: consistent with an unsquared factor), and the sentence is a valid corollary of that wrong (3.8) (C8). No missing datum explains it and no new datum would change it. Evidence the other way -- that the error matters for the physics KF drew: it does not overturn the qualitative conclusion; the exact bound is 1/3 < Delta < 1 on rho < 0 (C6), fluctuations of order unity, and later work (Ford-Roman gr-qc/9410043; Perez-Sudarsky 2512.17789) carried forward only that qualitative conclusion. The criterion itself was later narrowed on physical, not data, grounds (Hu-Roura-Verdaguer gr-qc/0402029: back-reaction must be included).
grade_evidence: Graded on KF's printed inequality in arXiv v1 ('rho < 0 ... In this case we have Delta(x) > 1'), with Delta as KF define it in (3.2). A computed contradiction is SHOWN here, not a misprint: with the exact Delta = |1 - (2eps - sqrt2 cos2th)^2/(3(1+eps^2))| (exact Fock matrices, C2-C3, (2.12)-(2.14) recovered from (2.11), C1), z3 proves that NO state of the family has rho < 0 and Delta > 1 (C5, vacuity guard SAT), and in fact Delta < 1 at every rho < 0 point, 1/3 < Delta < 1 tight (C6); the tree's witness eps = 1/10, theta = 0 (exact 0.5134 vs (3.8) 2.0118) is one instance of a universal failure. It is not a typographical slip of the sentence: the sentence follows validly from KF's (3.8) (C8), and (3.8) is not reproduced by any combination of KF's own printed lines (C7) -- an algebraic error, consistent with an unsquared factor (C9, mechanism not established). Weight, both ways: (i) the tree's recorded use -- KF_CLAIM_NEGATIVE_MEANS_DELTA_GT_1 = False, 'refuted', scoped to v1 (fluctuation.py:55-64, 143, 309-312, 478-479) -- is CONFIRMED and sharpened (the tree says 'a counterexample'; the failure is everywhere on rho < 0); (ii) KF's QUALITATIVE conclusion survives exactly as the tree records (KF_QUALITATIVE_CONCLUSION_SURVIVES = True, fluctuation.py:152): Delta > 1/3, order unity, wherever rho < 0 -- so the error gives no relief to negative-energy semiclassics and nothing here is in M's favour; (iii) scope: v1 text layer only -- PRD 47, 4510 is NAMED-NOT-READ and the page image was not viewed, so nothing here says the journal version prints the same inequality. Residual named limits: this stage read a cached harvest of the alphaXiv v1 text (fresh fetch refused: quota / egress 403); discover_papers was quota-refused, so the later-literature record is from cached texts only.
what_would_change_the_grade: To OPEN (for v1): the v1 page image showing a different (3.8) or a different inequality in the sentence than the text layer gives (implausible: the extracted (3.8) and '>' are mutually consistent and the next sentence requires '>', C8). To a narrower SCOPE, not a different grade: reading PRD 47, 4510 -- if the journal prints a corrected (3.8) and drops 'Delta > 1', the WRONG applies to v1 only (as the tree already scopes it). To NARROWED: a different state or definition of Delta under which KF's family was meant (e.g. Delta without normal ordering of T00^2, or a multimode vac+2 state) that the text does not state -- none is indicated at p.4-6. Nothing computable moves it: C4-C6 are z3 proofs over all real eps and all theta.
